title: Tonle Sap study window
description: A schematic study window for exploring the interface while the data team prepares real observations.
method: Deterministic geometric shapes generated for interface testing. No SAR processing, detection, or environmental analysis has been performed.

properties.meaning: Synthetic display footprint, not validated observation coverage

change.label: Schematic added shape — not detected inundation

observed: Two schematic views illustrate how a prepared observation pair will appear. Shapes and differences were deliberately drawn for this development example.
explanation: Use the divider or Before and After controls to inspect the pair. The brighter example overlay is a drawn shape, not a detected flood or a radar-derived measurement.
limitations: No real NISAR acquisitions are included.
Dates and viewpoints are illustrative; this is not a confirmed flood case.
Seasonal inundation and damaging flooding require independent contextual evidence.

sources.title: NISAR Data User Guide — background reference
Dancing with the SARs — official challenge

story.title: Start with a place.
story.body: This illustrative window is positioned near Tonle Sap. Its rectangle demonstrates how actual observation coverage will be displayed. The study area is not finalized.

story.title: Look across two moments.
story.body: Slide between these schematic frames to try the comparison. Real observations must use compatible measurements, geometry, and display settings before differences can be interpreted.

story.title: Leave room for uncertainty.
story.body: A difference starts an investigation. Supporting evidence is needed to distinguish seasonal water patterns from flooding. This development case makes no environmental finding.
